_readme: This contract is the single source of truth for worker wire vocabulary. It defines persisted notification types, the notification-thread discriminator, shared Codex rate-limit tokens, and model sentinels. The generator emits the Go NotificationType constants and the TypeScript NOTIFICATION_TYPE table. workerWrittenNotificationTypes lists notifications that only the Worker writes. The browser uses this list to identify standalone rows. Move a type between regimes only by editing this contract. Add a notification type here, then run task generate. Both dispatch switches then compile against the generated value. GoalUpdated and GoalCleared are worker-written by design. Each provider that reports a goal uses its own wire shape. The Worker normalizes each shape into one neutral row, so the browser keeps one goal renderer. goalStatusTokens and goalTransitions define separate payload vocabularies. goal_status stores the neutral state. goal_transition states the change that occurred. notificationRenderers reads both values for the transcript line. Before this contract, Go and TypeScript each defined these values. The agents.goal_status column does not store these tokens. It stores the AgentGoalStatus ordinal, and enum_column_numbering_test.go checks its CHECK range. Separate transition tokens distinguish changes that end at the same state. For example, a first set and a resume both end at active. The applier uses the prior row to select the transition. goalTransitionKind must produce every transition token in this contract. Add a token only with the branch that writes it. AgentStatus is worker-written for the same normalization reason. Goose sends a status_message notice, while Reasonix sends a session phase. The Worker converts both into one status row. A status row carries only text because the status is a sentence. SubagentReport is worker-written because providers expose reports through different channels. The Worker mirrors each report into its owning transcript. It also adds a parent row when the provider's parent result omits the report. InputRequeued is worker-written because the input queue writes it. A provider hands back a message that the agent accepted during a turn and then dropped before the model read it. The Worker queues that message again and writes this row, so the reader learns why the same message appears twice. notificationFields defines each payload key that the Worker writes and the browser reads. This includes type, label, old_label, and new_label. The envelope discriminator previously appeared beside generated notification types at 31 Go writers. Every value uses snake_case, and the schema rejects other forms. This table selects each wire key, and Go struct tags follow it. New entries cannot select a separate convention. The goal fields stay in one table because goal_transition prevents a resumed goal from appearing new. The comment in output_goal.go documents this invariant. Renaming only that key restores the regression.
